description: Swamp-green and faintly gritty, with things suspended in it you would rather not name.
lore: The grit is why anyone buys it. Every glob out of a crossing is a squeeze of that crossing's bottom, so the fen stalls press each one flat between two boards before it goes in the jar, on the strength of what has come out over the years: teeth, buttons, fish-hooks, a brass hinge, coins from four centuries in one afternoon, and once a walker's ring out of a shallow [[monsters/mystical_frog|the frog]] has held since before the roads were where they are.

A woman comes to that market and asks to do the pressing herself. She buys none of it. She lost something at a ford a long time ago and can no longer say what it was, only that her hands will know it when they find it. Everyone lets her press. She is Bright by every measure the trade has, she has been coming for four years, and the stall keeps her boards behind the counter.
gm_notes: Thinning shown from outside on an ordinary market day: not a shape at Habit, just a careful woman searching for a thing whose description has already gone. Do not diagnose her at the table; the boards behind the counter say everything.
